question: Which of the following was the first B vitamin discovered in 1897 that is essential in amino acid and carbohydrate metabolism and is active in energy production reactions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thiamine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thiamine, **also referred to as **vitamin B1,** was the initial B vitamin identified in **1897**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in amino acid and carbohydrate metabolism, contributing to energy production reactions.
 
• This essential nutrient is present in both plants and animals, facilitating the conversion of glucose into energy.
 
• Additionally, thiamine contributes to nerve function and aids in regulating basic metabolism within cells.
 
• A diverse range of processed and whole foods contains thiamine, including lentils, peas, whole grains, pork, and nuts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biotin, **a member of the B vitamin family, plays a vital role in numerous metabolic processes in both humans and other organisms. Its functions primarily revolve around the utilization of fats, carbohydrates, and amino acids.
 
• **Riboflavin**, also recognized as vitamin B2, is a water-soluble vitamin belonging to the B complex. Crucial for the synthesis of two coenzymes, flavin mononucleotide and flavin adenine dinucleotide, it supports various metabolic activities.
 
• **Folate,** another B vitamin, is naturally present in numerous foods. It is indispensable for DNA and genetic material synthesis, as well as cell division processes within the body.
